properties.label: Down length
properties.conditions: one study of grey and black yak down

timeline.event: Untargeted proteomics identified 156 proteins in yak fiber against 174 in cashmere and 157 in wool, supporting species discrimination.
Measurements on Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau family yak farms found methane and nitrous oxide made up about two-thirds of annual global warming potential.
An ultrasonic, melanin-targeted Fenton bleaching method raised yak hair whiteness index from about 11 to 45 with about 15% tensile strength loss.
A yak grazing experiment on the eastern Tibetan Plateau found heavier grazing reduced ecosystem multifunctionality.

properties.label: Comfort factor
properties.conditions: share of fibers at or below 30 microns, 60 French Angora rabbits, OFDA

timeline.event: An OFDA study of 349 fleece samples from French Angora rabbits characterized fineness, comfort factor and medullation.
Regulation (EU) No 1007/2011 listed angora in Annex I as a fiber name reserved for Angora rabbit hair.
After a PETA Asia video of hair being ripped from rabbits on Chinese farms, many retailers suspended or ended angora sales.
A homozygous missense mutation in the FGF5 gene was associated with the long-hair trait in all tested Angora rabbits.

properties.label: Mean fiber diameter
properties.conditions: 22 fiber samples, three communities in southeastern Peru

timeline.event: The vicuna was listed in CITES Appendix I when the Convention entered into force on 1 July, barring primarily commercial international trade.
Certain vicuna populations in Chile and Peru were transferred to CITES Appendix II at the sixth Conference of the Parties.
The remaining Peruvian populations were transferred to Appendix II, for trade in fiber shorn from live animals.
Certain populations in Argentina and Bolivia were transferred to Appendix II.
The US Fish and Wildlife Service reclassified certain vicuna populations from endangered to threatened with a special rule.
A scoping review documented sarcoptic mange outbreaks, with prevalence up to about 60% in some vicuna populations.

timeline.event: The two-humped (Bactrian) camel was domesticated, according to archaeological dating.
The US Wool Products Labeling Act allowed camel hair to be treated as a specialty fiber within its wool definition.
Genetic analysis showed the living wild camel is a separate lineage rather than the direct ancestor of domestic Bactrians.
A chamber study including Bactrian camels found lower methane per kilogram of body mass than in roughage-fed ruminants.

timeline.event: A study of free-ranging guanacos measured rises in glucocorticoid stress hormones with handling, shearing and release.
A 36-year population series from Tierra del Fuego found that sheep density strongly depressed guanaco population growth.
Surveys estimated about 1.1 million guanacos in Santa Cruz province, Argentina (95% CI 0.7 to 1.6 million).
Research documented conflict between farmers and the critically endangered guanaco population of southern Peru.

timeline.event: Fleece samples were taken from 299 wild muskox hides during the November Banks Island harvest for the first standardized qiviut fiber study.
Mass mortality events linked to one clone of Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae struck muskoxen on Banks, Victoria and Prince Patrick Islands.
Qiviut cortisol was validated as a measure of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity in muskoxen.
Trace and macro element profiles of qiviut were shown to reflect muskox population trends.
